_comment: Direct pull of every real Figma VARIABLE in Mozilla's authoritative 'Nova Styles
(Experimental)' file (key Co6vXnF5SiQMcJ7UoJvZX6), via a single unauthenticated-
except-for-a-token REST call: GET /v1/files/{FILE_ID}/variables/local. This
REPLACES an earlier Supernova-MCP-sourced dump (see git history for
figma-token-dump.json) that the repo maintainer rejected as the wrong source for
this check: Supernova's sync of this file is known to have gaps elsewhere in this
project family (it mislabeled its own source file as 'Desktop Styles' and could
not confirm it was even the same file as 'Nova Styles'), so token-existence checks
against Figma must hit the Figma REST API directly, never Supernova. This is the
exact file/endpoint prototype/design-system/scripts/gen_tokens_css.py in the
sibling ai-native-ux-hub repo already pulls from to generate that project's own
tokens.css, confirmed by reading that script directly rather than assumed.
This is a FULL dump: every one of the file's 720 raw variables across all 9
variable collections in the file (HCM Theme, Theme, Operating System, Surface,
Colors x2 [one is a single remote/external-library alias target, kept because it
is still a real resolvable entry in this file], Primitives, Tab Group Theme,
Components), minus the 2 variables Figma itself flags 'deletedButReferenced'
(background/color/box/accent/primary, border/color/overlay): these no longer
exist as live variables, only as dangling references something else still points
at, so counting them as 'exists in Figma' would be a false positive. Only `name`,
`type` (resolvedType), `collection`, and `remote` are kept per variable -- values,
modes, aliasing, and descriptions are dropped because figma-check.py's matching is
purely name-based and doesn't need them (see figma-check.py's own docstring for
why). Re-running the fetch (see token-api/README.md's 'Figma existence check'
section) regenerates this file from scratch; there is no incremental update path.
codeSyntax was checked here too, the same way the earlier Supernova pass checked
it, not assumed unusable just because the prior connection lacked it: this direct
Figma API response DOES include a `codeSyntax` field per variable, but only 2 of
720 have it populated (button/background/color, tab/border/color), nowhere near
enough to be a general match signal. Matching is still by normalized name, exactly
as before; see figma-check.py's docstring for the exact rule.
